SEQUENCING FINDING: 9ce8 is not workable yet, and the graph is right.

rebar ready lists 9ce8 with no direct blockers, but claiming it triggers the parent-first cascade onto its parent 373f (comment triage), which this epic's dependency edges block behind 15 point fixes. So 9ce8 is effectively blocked by its PARENT even though its own blocker set is empty. That is the intended ordering -- comment triage must read final code, not code about to change -- but it means 'ready' overstates the frontier for any child of a blocked parent. Worth knowing when picking work here.

THROUGHPUT NOTE for whoever continues: the binding constraint on this epic is not implementation effort, it is the serialized LLM gate pipeline. Plan review, completion verification and code review each take 10-40 minutes, they all contend on one store write lock, and origin/main advances faster than a review completes -- which stales attestations mid-flight. Two workarounds proven here:
  (a) run review-plan and claim back-to-back in ONE shell invocation, and
  (b) when an attestation is already stale, pin the worktree to the exact SHA it was signed at
      (git checkout --detach <verified_at_sha>) and claim from there, rather than re-reviewing.
Also: tick AC boxes and add any [operator-attested] tags BEFORE running review-plan. Editing the
description afterwards stales the attestation and the close gate rejects it -- a catch-22 that cost
two extra review cycles on ae96 and 723f.
